governanceNotes: Authored conservatively at ASSOCIATION_ONLY strength: the single controlled study (Thomas 2022, 45 cases vs 90 controls) documents a strong tracheomalacia-bronchiectasis association (adjusted OR 13.2-24.4), but it is pediatric, single-center, age-imbalanced by design, and its authors explicitly disclaim causality.

Shared-terrain confounder recorded: connective-tissue disease literature documents TBM and bronchiectasis as parallel structural and inflammatory manifestations within Ehlers-Danlos syndromes (Bascom 2021), and COPD/smoking confounds the adult literature, so either shared-substrate structure defeats a simple causal reading.

Supersedes the batch-6 automation deferral (2026-09-22, same day): that deferral withheld an edge because the screened adult recurrent-infection literature was confounded by the shared COPD/smoking substrate and asked to revisit only with collapse-specific evidence; the Thomas 2022 pediatric case-control is tracheomalacia-specific, bronchoscopy-verified against controls, and free of the smoking confound, satisfying the deferral's own reopening condition. The deferral's broader caution is preserved in the edge guards (no causality, shared-substrate alternatives listed).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: A single-center case-control study (45 CT-confirmed bronchiectasis cases vs 90 disease controls, bronchoscopy videos reviewed blinded) found any tracheomalacia significantly associated with bronchiectasis (adjusted OR 13.2, 95% CI 3.2-55) and ERS-defined tracheomalacia further increasing that estimate (ORadj 24.4, 95% CI 3.4-infinity), with the authors explicitly concluding that causality cannot be inferred (Thomas 2022); the Ehlers-Danlos respiratory review documents tracheobronchomalacia as a structural manifestation and bronchiectasis as an inflammatory manifestation within the same syndrome population (Bascom 2021); the spirometry 'knee'-pattern study documents tracheomalacia in 65.4% of pattern-positive children, supporting case-finding context (Boonjindasup 2022).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the only controlled association comes from a pediatric single-center case-control design with age imbalance between groups, its authors explicitly disclaim causality, shared inflammatory and connective-tissue substrates can generate both conditions in parallel, and post-infectious causes dominate adult bronchiectasis, so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: An impaired-clearance/chronic-infection pathway is hypothesized: excessive expiratory collapse of the tracheobronchial walls impairs mucociliary transport and cough-mediated secretion expectoration, promoting chronic bacterial colonization and neutrophilic airway inflammation, which drive the bronchial-wall remodeling that defines bronchiectasis; the same vicious-cycle biology that maintains bronchiectasis is plausibly initiated or amplified by the mechanical clearance failure. The mechanism is physiologically coherent and is the working hypothesis of the case-control literature, but no longitudinal incidence data establish the progression rate in bronchomalacia populations, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Tracheobronchomalacia is strongly associated with bronchiectasis in the one controlled study available; individual determination requires CT documentation of bronchiectasis, bronchoscopic grading of airway collapse with chronology, exclusion of post-infectious and systemic causes, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Chest high-resolution CT documenting bronchiectasis with lobar distribution; bronchoscopic grading of expiratory airway collapse (ERS >50% criterion) with chronology relative to bronchiectasis onset; documentation of recurrent wet cough and infection history bridging the two conditions; workup excluding primary ciliary dyskinesia, immunodeficiency, cystic fibrosis, prior necrotizing infection, and connective-tissue disease; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Post-infectious bronchiectasis (pneumonia, adenovirus, tuberculosis) independent of airway collapse
COPD and smoking as a shared substrate for both conditions
Primary ciliary dyskinesia causing both impaired clearance and bronchiectasis
Ehlers-Danlos or other connective-tissue disease producing both manifestations in parallel

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the association estimate is large but rests on one pediatric case-control whose authors disclaim causality, and the shared-substrate alternatives are well documented; the edge records co-occurrence only and leaves every causal judgment to a qualified medical professional.
